title: Wait for Bluetooth before starting its agent
author: yashranaway
body:
Keeps Bluetooth pairing available when the user session starts before `bluetooth.service`. Fixes #8962.

<<<< AI wording below >>>>

## Problem

The user unit checks the system Bluetooth service with `ExecCondition`. A failed condition is a clean, permanent skip, so a three-second boot race can leave the pairing agent absent for the whole session.

## Fix

Wait up to 30 seconds for the system service in `ExecStartPre`. A timeout is a real service failure, so the existing restart policy retries it, with systemd start limits bounding repeated failures.

## Verification

- `bash test/shell.d/systemd-test.sh`
- `bash test/shell.d/bluetooth-test.sh`
- `git diff --check`
- `systemd-analyze verify` parsed the unit but could not complete because this checkout does not have `/usr/bin/bt-agent` or its man page.

files.patch:
@@ -5,12 +5,14 @@ ConditionPathIsDirectory=/sys/class/bluetooth
 # bluez must be reachable on the system bus before we can register.
 After=dbus.socket
 Requires=dbus.socket
+StartLimitIntervalSec=120
+StartLimitBurst=3
 
 [Service]
 Type=simple
-# If bluetoothd is unavailable (for example in VMs or machines without a
-# usable adapter), skip cleanly instead of entering a restart loop.
-ExecCondition=/usr/bin/systemctl is-active --quiet bluetooth.service
+# The user manager cannot order this unit after the system manager's Bluetooth
+# service, so wait through the normal boot race instead of skipping forever.
+ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/timeout 30 /bin/bash -c 'until /usr/bin/systemctl is-active --quiet bluetooth.service; do sleep 1; done'
 # NoInputNoOutput auto-accepts pair requests. Safe because the adapter
 # is only `pairable: true` when the user explicitly opens the omarchy
 # bluetoothPanel and starts scanning; outside that window bluez refuses

@@ -6,8 +6,14 @@ source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
 
 service="$ROOT/default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service"
 
-grep -Fx 'ExecCondition=/usr/bin/systemctl is-active --quiet bluetooth.service' "$service" >/dev/null
-pass "bt-agent skips when bluetooth.service is inactive"
+grep -Fx "ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/timeout 30 /bin/bash -c 'until /usr/bin/systemctl is-active --quiet bluetooth.service; do sleep 1; done'" "$service" >/dev/null ||
+  fail "bt-agent waits for the system Bluetooth service during login"
+if grep -q '^ExecCondition=.*bluetooth.service' "$service"; then
+  fail "bt-agent no longer turns an early Bluetooth check into a permanent skip"
+fi
+grep -Fx 'StartLimitIntervalSec=120' "$service" >/dev/null || fail "bt-agent bounds failed startup retries"
+grep -Fx 'StartLimitBurst=3' "$service" >/dev/null || fail "bt-agent bounds failed startup retries"
+pass "bt-agent waits through the system service startup race"
 
 grep -Fx 'Restart=on-failure' "$service" >/dev/null
 pass "bt-agent still restarts after runtime failures"
